titleEn: Split in Two, Share a Bite!

pages.text: "The last apricot!" Lulu quickly took the yellow fruit from the plate. Three cousins watched from the doorway. Lulu hid it behind the back. "I will eat it all."
Three blunt hands reached out. "One bite for us too, Lulu." Lulu turned away and went beneath the table. "No. There is only one."
The cousins stayed in the doorway, watching. Below the table, Lulu stared at the apricot. Strangely, eating alone made it hard to open the mouth.
Mom peered below. "Our Lulu has an apricot. Why so sad?" Lulu's ears drooped. "Eating alone is not tasty at all."
Mom took it and pressed with her hands. Pop! Two halves, one stone in the middle. "See? Split it, and there are two."
Lulu pressed the halves again. Pop, pop! Now four. Wide eyes, a jingling bell. "Split in two, share a bite!"
Lulu ran into the yard with the plate. "Let us eat together!" Three cousins turned at once beneath the olive tree.
Lulu set a piece in each hand—one, another, another. Four sat side by side, chewing. "Much tastier than eating alone!" a cousin said.
At dinner, one piece of bread remained. Lulu pressed it in both hands and split it. "One, ask first! Two, split it! Three, give everyone a piece!"
Mom lifted Lulu in a tight hug. Sharing food is tastier and more fun. Lulu rubbed a face against her apron. "Split in two, share a bite!"
